column1: # Training cutoffs, read from each model's own publication or repository
# rather than from a secondary source. 02_build_holdout_set.py reads this file
# and takes the latest cutoff as the common one, so that a single held-out set
# is out of training for every model compared. Changing a date here changes the
# set, which is the point: the dates are evidence, not constants in a script.
# date_basis is the column that decides whether the filter is sound. A model
# that selected its training examples by deposition date is not protected by a
# release-date filter, because a structure released in 2024 may have been
# deposited in 2021 and held. Both dates are recorded per target and the
# stricter one is used, so this column says what each model claims rather than
# leakage_note carries what the date cannot cover. Both models were trained on
# predicted structures as well as deposited ones, and a target whose sequence
# or a close homologue appeared in that predicted data is not unseen in any
# useful sense, whatever its deposition date. No filter here can exclude that.

column4: Jumper et al. 2021, Nature 596:583-589, Methods, Training regimen
column5: To train, we use structures from the PDB with a maximum release date of 30 April 2018
column6: 75 per cent of training examples were the model's own predictions of 355,993 Uniclust30 v2018_08 sequences, so sequence-level exposure is not excluded by a structure date

column4: Boltz-2 technical report, bioRxiv 2025.06.14.659707, Data section and Appendix A.1.1
column6: distillation used about five million AlphaFold Database monomers and further self-distillation sets, so the same caveat applies more strongly
